- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially if recent prices are rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >70), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to avoid excessive overshoot.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in early forecast periods (e.g., 30d horizon) — if true outcome deviates sharply from recent mean, adjust forecast toward historical volatility range.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to smooth out extremes; consider adding a small volatility buffer to forecast to capture sentiment-driven noise.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a spike, model often fails to recognize it — adjust downward more aggressively if sentiment turns negative.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts — if sentiment changes sharply within 5–7 days, adjust forecast to reflect recent sentiment direction.
